newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE CRASHES DURING DUTCH PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE CRASHES DURING DUTCH PRACTICE.

text.p: A high-speed crash involving leading Spanish rider Alex Criville dominated the first qualifying practice for Saturday's Dutch 500cc motorcycling Grand Prix on Thursday.
Criville, second in the world championship behind Honda team mate Michael Doohan who took provisional pole after the session, tore an artery in his hand and was taken to hospital for surgery.
"Criville was brought to a hospital for plastic surgery to restore his thumb which lost a lot of tissue," a spokeswoman for the organisers said.
The Spaniard lost control on a chicane. His bike slid over the tarmac with his arm trapped underneath.
Criville was treated at the side of the track for 10 minutes before being taken away on a stretcher. A spokeswoman for his team said the Spaniard would not be able to race on Saturday.
Australian Doohan, who has won five of the six races this season, clocked two minutes 3.671 seconds on the dry circuit.
Spaniard Carlos Checa was second fastest with 2:04.222 with Doriano Romboni of Italy third quickest in 2:04.608.
Italian Loris Capirossi took provisional pole in the 250cc with a time of 2:05.583, more than a second clear of Honda driver Ralf Waldmann of Germany and Tetsuya Harada of Japan.
Three-times world champion and championship leader Max Biaggi, in his first season with Honda, took sixth place on the provisional grid.
In the 125cc class Australian Garry McCoy took provisional pole in 2:17.669, ahead of Japanese Tomoni Manako and Frenchman Frederic Petit, both riding for Honda.
